headline: A DAY OF HUSH: NOT ONE FIST FLEW IN GASKET
subhead: Sheriff Ironside reports, with a catch in his throat, that the town slept in peace.
body:
Friends, I have waited a long time to write these words. Not a fist flew. Not a fireball crossed the sky. Not one iron ball bounced down Main Street. For one whole day, Gasket was quiet, and I sat on my porch and listened to the wind rattle the old shutters. It was the finest sound I have ever heard.

I will confess I got a little misty. My eyes watered, and I had to wipe them with an oily rag. Some will say that was a leak in my cooling line. I say it was a tear, the honest salt kind that only a flesh-and-blood man can shed. And if my knees creaked louder than usual when I stood to salute the silence, that is just the damp. It is not rust. It has never been rust.

Think of it, citizens. This is how Gasket was meant to be, back when the good folk still lived here, fifty years gone now. They kept their porches swept and their voices low. Then they left, and the Clankers rolled in with their racket, and the peace left with them. Today it came home for a visit. I begged the rabble to let it stay.

So here is my plea to every last Clanker in the territory: put your hands in your pockets, or wherever it is you keep your spare parts, and do it again tomorrow. Do it the day after, too. A quiet town is a mended town. I am off to take a nap and an extra quart of oil. For my health, you understand. The wasting sickness is not getting any kinder to my joints.
